identity.title: Your Mixture-of-Experts LLM Is Secretly an Embedding Model for Free

problem.claim: The study asks whether MoE LLM components can provide useful text embeddings without additional representation finetuning.

gap.claim: Decoder-only LLM architecture is described as limiting embedding use when representation finetuning is absent.

contributions.claim: An off-the-shelf MoE expert router is used as an embedding model without finetuning.
Routing weights are reported as complementary to hidden states, more prompt-robust, and focused on high-level semantics relative to hidden states.
MoEE combines routing weights and hidden states, with a weighted sum of their similarities outperforming similarity on their concatenation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present novel insights about combining MoE routing weights, hidden states, and prompting, including the advantage of weighted similarity combination over concatenation similarity.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report promising performance from expert-router embeddings across diverse embedding-focused tasks without finetuning.
The authors report experiments on 6 embedding tasks spanning 20 MTEB datasets.
The authors report that MoEE significantly improves LLM-based embedding without further finetuning.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM decoder-only architecture is presented as a limitation for embedding use without representation finetuning.
The study frames a generalist-model question and examines MoE LLMs.
Expert routers are presented as usable off-the-shelf embeddings; routing weights are analyzed against hidden states for complementarity, prompt robustness, and semantic focus.
MoEE combines routing weights and hidden states, with a weighted similarity strategy reported as superior to concatenation similarity.
The authors report evaluation across 6 tasks and 20 MTEB datasets, with significant improvement from MoEE without finetuning.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links an analysis of routing weights versus hidden states to the design of MoEE and specifies that weighted similarity combination outperforms concatenation similarity.

lessons.interpretation: A component-level analysis can motivate a targeted composition rule rather than treating representations as interchangeable.
lessons.application: When combining embedding signals, compare fusion operators explicitly and connect the selected operator to observed differences in robustness or semantic content.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when the available evidence does not distinguish component behavior or when the application requires a single representation with no tunable fusion stage.

unknowns: The abstract gives no numerical results, task-level breakdown, model identities, or comparator details, so the magnitude and scope of the reported improvements are unspecified.
The basis and evaluation conditions for claims such as “promising,” “more robust,” and “significant” are not detailed.
